about: Rockhound Scout field list: which FORMATIONS produce which materials, by state. Not a list of spots. 'high' = documented producer; 'possible' = may contain it. Rows marked authoritative (JT's field knowledge) override the AI; researched rows can only raise the AI's rating. Patterns are case-insensitive text patterns; | means 'or'. Optional 'areas' = [[lat, lon, miles], ...] limits a row to searches near those places. 'review' marks rows that need a stronger source before launch.
generalNote: Public land rules (most BLM land): reasonable personal amounts of rocks, minerals and common invertebrate or plant fossils; petrified wood up to 25 lb plus 1 piece per day and 250 lb per year; no vertebrate fossils (bones, teeth, tracks); no collecting in national parks, developed recreation sites, or on mining claims without the claimholder's permission.

stateNotes.Hawaii: Hawaii is one of the most restrictive states for collecting. State rules prohibit taking sand, rocks, dead coral or other beach deposits from the shoreline (shells, driftwood and beach glass are allowed). Collecting is prohibited in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park and at Papakolea green-sand beach, and most zeolite outcrops are on private or military land. Many visitors photograph rather than collect.
stateNotes.Alaska: No rock, mineral or fossil collecting in national parks (the Kobuk jade country borders Gates of the Arctic). Alaska Native corporation land is private. Never pan or dig on an active mining claim without the claimholder's written permission; recreational panning is allowed on most open state and BLM land.
stateNotes.Nevada: Much of Nevada is BLM land open to casual collecting, but mining claims are everywhere — you can't collect on an active claim without the claimant's permission. Most turquoise mines are closed to the public.
stateNotes.Colorado: Much of the Pikes Peak crystal country is National Forest, but active mining claims are common and some areas (like Crystal Park) are largely private — never dig on a claim without permission.
stateNotes.Kansas: Nearly all of Kansas is private land — fossil hunting there needs the landowner's permission.
stateNotes.Nebraska: Most of Nebraska is private land. On Oglala National Grassland, personal rock collecting is allowed under casual-use rules; vertebrate fossils need a federal permit.
stateNotes.South Dakota: No collecting of any kind inside Badlands National Park or Wind Cave/Mount Rushmore. Buffalo Gap National Grassland allows surface collecting of minerals and common invertebrate fossils for personal use.
stateNotes.North Dakota: No collecting in Theodore Roosevelt National Park. Little Missouri National Grassland: 25 lb per day, 250 lb per year, no machinery, no vertebrate fossils.
stateNotes.Wisconsin: Collecting rocks, minerals and fossils is prohibited in Wisconsin State Parks.
stateNotes.Michigan: Collecting is prohibited at Isle Royale, Pictured Rocks and Sleeping Bear Dunes (National Park Service). Michigan limits collecting on state land to 25 lb.

rows.label: zeolite crystals
rows.note: Zeolites fill gas pockets in weathered basalt on the older islands (mainly Oahu and Kauai); most known outcrops are on private or military land.

rows.label: petrified wood
rows.high: chinle|shinarump|sonsela|petrified forest member|blue mesa|owl rock|painted desert member
rows.note: No collecting in Petrified Forest National Park. On BLM land: up to 25 lb plus 1 piece per day, 250 lb per year.

rows.label: thundereggs
rows.note: Many famous thunderegg beds are fee-dig ranches (e.g. Priday, Richardson's); some public sites need permits — check before digging.

rows.label: quartz crystals
rows.note: Many Ouachita crystal sites are pay-to-dig mines near Mount Ida and Jessieville — call ahead for fees.

rows.label: diamonds
rows.note: Crater of Diamonds State Park: pay a small fee and keep what you find.

rows.label: Lake Superior agates
rows.note: Agates formed in the North Shore lava flows; glaciers spread them through gravels across NE and central Minnesota.

rows.label: topaz crystals
rows.note: Topaz Mountain is a BLM rockhound area; topaz fades from amber to clear in sunlight.

rows.label: dinosaur bone (look, don't take on public land)
rows.note: Vertebrate fossils such as dinosaur bone can't be collected on federal land; only on private land with the owner's permission.

rows.label: thundereggs, agate and jasper
rows.note: Rockhound State Park (near Deming) allows collecting up to 15 lb per visitor; no collecting for resale.

rows.label: barite rose rocks
rows.note: Rose rocks occur mainly from just northeast of Lexington to north of Lake Stanley Draper, around Norman.

rows.label: nephrite jade
rows.note: Jade Cove area (Big Sur): loose jade may be collected only below mean high tide, by hand, and only what one person can carry; day use only.
rows.review: host rock not named in source; listed as possible only

rows.label: precious opal
rows.note: Virgin Valley opal: private fee-dig mines (e.g. Royal Peacock, Bonanza) surrounded by BLM land.

rows.label: trilobites
rows.review: Oak Springs trilobite area is BLM shale; formation name (Pioche Shale) not confirmed by source

rows.label: star garnets
rows.note: Emerald Creek star garnet area (Idaho Panhandle National Forests): advance tickets required through recreation.gov.
rows.review: source rock not named in source; possible only

rows.label: sapphires
rows.note: Montana sapphires: fee digs on the Missouri River bars near Helena (e.g. Spokane Bar) and at Gem Mountain on Rock Creek, where you buy and wash gravel.

rows.label: Montana moss agates
rows.note: Montana moss agates are found along the Yellowstone River and its tributaries; best at low water (early spring, late fall). A Montana Conservation License is needed for most state land, including fishing access sites.

rows.label: turritella (Elimia) agate
rows.review: forum source; confirm with a survey publication before launch

rows.label: fossil fish (look, don't take on public land)
rows.note: Fossil fish: no collecting at Fossil Butte National Monument; private quarries near Kemmerer offer fee digs. Vertebrate fossils can't be collected on federal land.

rows.label: petrified wood
rows.note: Ginkgo Petrified Forest State Park (Vantage) is for viewing; check state park rules before collecting anything.
rows.review: source names only the Columbia basalt group; listed as possible

rows.label: Eocene leaf and insect fossils
rows.note: Stonerose Interpretive Center (Republic): dig for your own fossils and take some home, under the center's rules.
rows.review: formation name (Klondike Mountain Fm) not in source

rows.label: almandine garnet
rows.note: Wrangell Garnet Ledge is privately owned; ask locally about permission.

rows.label: Cretaceous chalk fossils (oysters, giant clams, shark teeth)
rows.note: Western Kansas chalk is almost all private land (Monument Rocks and Castle Rock are private property open to visitors) — get the landowner's permission before collecting; bones of swimming reptiles and fish are best left to museums.
rows.review: carlile/graneros/dakota as 'possible' is my addition, not from the source

rows.label: Pennsylvanian–Permian fossils (crinoids, brachiopods, fusulinids)
rows.note: Eastern Kansas limestones and shales; road cuts are the classic exposures. Private land needs the owner's permission.
rows.review: group names in 'possible' are mine (standard Kansas group names); the source says eastern-Kansas Pennsylvanian/Permian rocks generally

rows.label: blue chalcedony (state gem), Fairburn and prairie agates
rows.note: Oglala National Grassland: personal rock and mineral collecting allowed under casual-use rules, no mechanized tools; vertebrate fossils need a federal permit.

rows.label: petrified wood
rows.note: Mostly small pieces in Ogallala gravels, Pine Ridge drainages and Platte River gravels.

rows.label: Fairburn and prairie agates
rows.note: Agate beds between Fairburn and Scenic, along French Creek and the Cheyenne River. Buffalo Gap National Grassland allows surface collecting of minerals and common invertebrate fossils for personal use; no collecting at all inside Badlands National Park.

rows.label: rose quartz and pegmatite minerals (beryl, tourmaline, garnet)
rows.note: Keystone–Custer pegmatite district; many old mines are on private claims — ask first.

rows.label: placer gold
rows.note: Fine gold in northern Hills creeks such as Whitewood and Deadwood Creeks; lode gold and active claims are off-limits.

rows.label: petrified wood
rows.note: Little Missouri National Grassland: casual collecting, 25 lb per day and 250 lb per year, no machinery, no vertebrate fossils. Theodore Roosevelt National Park: no collecting of anything.

rows.label: Knife River flint
rows.note: Never found in its original bed; pieces turn up on Knife River and Spring Creek terraces in Dunn, Mercer and Oliver counties and in gravels near Bismarck–Mandan. The Knife River Indian Villages and quarry sites are protected.
rows.review: sources disagree on the parent unit (ND Geological Survey: Golden Valley Fm, Camels Butte Mbr; rockhounding.org: Bullion Creek) — listed both as possible

rows.label: geodes and crystal pockets (calcite, galena, druzy quartz)
rows.note: Southwest Wisconsin lead-zinc country (Grant County bluffs, Platteville, Mineral Point). Collecting is prohibited in Wisconsin State Parks.

rows.label: Ordovician and Silurian fossils (brachiopods, trilobites, corals)
rows.note: Collecting is prohibited in Wisconsin State Parks.
rows.review: source is a list of fossil-bearing units, not a ranking; all set to possible

rows.label: Petoskey stones (fossil coral)
rows.note: Michigan limits collecting on state land to 25 lb; no collecting at Sleeping Bear Dunes (National Park Service).
rows.review: 'possible' Traverse-area unit names are mine; source names Gravel Point Fm / Traverse Group

rows.label: Lake Superior agates
rows.note: Upper Peninsula beaches and gravels. No collecting at Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore or Isle Royale National Park.

rows.label: native copper, greenstone (chlorastrolite) and datolite
rows.note: Keweenaw mine dumps and beaches. Mine dump ownership varies — don't assume an unposted dump is open. Collecting is prohibited on Isle Royale.

rows.label: geodes
rows.note: South-central Indiana road cuts and creek beds (around Bloomington–Bedford).
rows.review: 'possible' units are neighboring units, not named as geode-bearing in the source
